races.name: Melissa, Arabella And Oriana Hawthorne Handicap

runners_data.name: Keats House
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with licence to dictate on Good turf, Easterby yard in 5/40 form over 14 days; style-fit tag of 0.93 reflects this is not its absolute optimum role but it is the natural pace-setter here by default, giving it a significant tactical advantage.
runners_data.comment: There is a sense of improving form about Keats House, and his latest effort at Redcar — fifth, beaten 5¼ lengths — showed some progression. He handles this distance and any going; if that upward curve continues he is not without a chance.

runners_data.name: Mayor Of Maghera
runners_data.note: Tudhope in the saddle for a yard that has cooled (0/14 T14) and the horse's stable form includes a 20f run suggesting stamina is not the issue; a genuine hold-up type that needs a proper gallop to produce its best, which this shape may not guarantee.
runners_data.comment: Beaten just 1¼ lengths off this very same mark at Ayr last time, Mayor Of Maghera showed enough to make him a solid contender here. First-time cheekpieces could sharpen him further, and he handles this trip on any ground; the mark looks fair.

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby yard is in strong form (16/98 T14) and this 4yo has two wins on Good ground at 8f in recent history — a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is at the rear, mapped to midfield only because of field congestion; will likely settle at the back regardless.
runners_data.comment: Perfidia landed a handicap by a length off this exact mark at Nottingham five days ago and comes here in first-time cheekpieces without a penalty. He handles this trip and going; the one caveat is that it was an apprentice contest, which tempers confidence slightly.

runners_data.name: Without Delay
runners_data.note: Veteran 7yo last seen 40 days ago and running off a career-low OR=47 for a yard with little current momentum (0/4 T14); a true hold-up type whose redistribution to midfield misrepresents where Waugh will likely place her — form figures of 0-0530 offer limited encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way at Catterick last time out, Without Delay needs to show a great deal more to be a factor here. She handles this trip on any ground and first-time cheekpieces are fitted, but her recent efforts offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie yard firing at 7/54 T14 and this 6yo has a win and a place on Good ground at 8f in its last five — the true hold-up style means Lauren Young will drop her in, and the step to 1m1f could help, but the redistribution flag signals she won't get the rails position she ideally needs.
runners_data.comment: Third when beaten a length off the same mark last time out, Approaching Dawn ran consistently for a stable that has won this race twice in the last five years. He acts on good ground at this trip, though his form can be variable; the conditions look right.

runners_data.name: Bay Dream Believer
runners_data.note: Jason Hart takes the mount on a 7yo who has all four recent wins over 10f, making this drop to 1m1f a concern; hold-up style suits a genuine gallop but the trip looks short and his Musselburgh record (9/15 similar-going) is only moderate.
runners_data.comment: Bay Dream Believer won at Pontefract off a 3lb lower mark and was reportedly denied a clear run last time, masking her true level. She handles this trip and goes on any ground; first-time hood adds interest, though the trainer's current run-rate is a concern.

runners_data.name: Second Fiddle
runners_data.note: No wins or places in 15 similar-going runs (0W0P) is a stark historical flag for Jardine's runner; the prominent style gives it a chance to track Keats House, but consecutive poor finishes and a stable leaking form (9/34 T14) combine to make this a speculative holding.
runners_data.comment: Better on the all-weather earlier in the year, Second Fiddle's turf mark now looks very stiff; fourth beaten 8 lengths at Hamilton last time confirmed as much. First-time tongue-tie is an unknown and a trainer in form gives her a small chance, but she has plenty to find.

races.paceDynamic: Keats House is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to press them, Joanna Mason should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 1m1f trip at Musselburgh. Second Fiddle carries prominent profile data but a string of double-figure finishes in similar company makes them an unlikely pace influence, meaning Keats House commands the tempo unchallenged. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate — Perfidia, Without Delay, and Approaching Dawn are all true hold-up horses pushed forward on the map; in practice they will likely be settled in rear, deepening the chasing pack behind the leader. This shape — a single uncontested pace-setter controlling a modest gallop on Good turf with chasers bunched behind — strongly favours hold-up horses with a genuine finishing kick who can produce a sustained late run, provided the tempo is honest enough to stretch the field in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Keats House Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Keats House dictates a measured pace from the front and no rival applies meaningful early pressure, the leader builds an unassailable rhythm.
scenarios.body: If Keats House dictates a measured pace from the front and no rival applies meaningful early pressure, the leader builds an unassailable rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Runners Reel Leader In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Keats House is genuinely strong enough through the middle of the race to open up the field and deliver a true end-to-end gallop.
scenarios.body: If the pace set by Keats House is genuinely strong enough through the middle of the race to open up the field and deliver a true end-to-end gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Second Fiddle or Mayor Of Maghera tracks Keats House closely and produces a well-timed challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Second Fiddle or Mayor Of Maghera tracks Keats House closely and produces a well-timed challenge inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide-Open Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and multiple hold-up horses arrive simultaneously, producing a blanket finish.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and multiple hold-up horses arrive simultaneously, producing a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Keats House holds every key: if Joanna Mason gets a clean break and no rival forces her to quicken early, the leader's ability to control tempo from the front is the single biggest race-shape determinant — watch whether anything pushes wide to press in the first two furlongs.

Perfidia, Without Delay, and Approaching Dawn are all natural rear-of-field horses crowded into midfield on the map — watch for a bunched group of hold-up horses tracking in a tight pack, which could cause trouble in running if the pace quickens suddenly on the turn.

Bay Dream Believer has recorded all four career wins over 10f and is dropping sharply to 1m1f — monitor whether Hart elects to hold up or press forward; if he chases Keats House hard he may compromise his own stamina-based profile.

Mayor Of Maghera switches from recent soft-ground efforts back to Good turf with Tudhope, who is a class booking for this yard — any market move would be noteworthy given the trainer's quiet recent spell (0/14 T14) and Tudhope's ability to galvanise horses in the right conditions.

runners_data.name: Just For Monty
runners_data.comment: Sprint-bred and still learning his trade, Just For Monty pulled too hard on soft ground at Ayr on debut and faded once that energy caught up with him. Better ground and this minimum trip should help, but he has plenty to prove at this stage.

runners_data.name: Turnstile
runners_data.comment: Consistent and dependable, Turnstile filled a place when a close third at York last time and handles this trip on a sound surface. While 5f on fast ground may bring out the best in him, his reliability gives him a clear edge in this field.

runners_data.name: Aodhan
runners_data.comment: Struggling to make an impression in either of his two starts so far, Aodhan has shown little promise and arrives here just three days after his latest below-par effort. Significant improvement is required to feature.

runners_data.name: Lexington Boom
runners_data.comment: An Ardad colt whose dam showed ability at 5f, Lexington Boom has the pedigree for this trip and represents a trainer in good form with a strong record in this race. A February foaling date means he is one of the younger runners, but his profile is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Bear Lee
runners_data.comment: Finishing fourth at Redcar on debut with a hint of late progress, Bear Lee hinted at better to come despite being held. She is speedily bred and a sound surface should suit her stride pattern; improvement looks likely with that experience under her belt.

runners_data.name: Heffernan Kingdom
runners_data.comment: Improved markedly on her second outing when third at Wetherby, having shown signs of inexperience when asked to lead earlier; a slight reduction in trip today looks well-timed, and she handles a sound surface. Further improvement looks within her grasp.

runners_data.name: Dadawada
runners_data.comment: A Kodiac filly and half-sister to a useful 6f performer, Dadawada was bought at a breeze-up for 18,000gns, with the sprint pedigree pointing to this trip. As an April foal making her debut, she is best watched initially, but the pedigree profile is encouraging.

races.name: Join Racing TV Now Handicap

runners_data.name: Marhaba Ghaiyyath
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with sole control of the pace here; good-going form is solid (9/13 similar ground) but a 59-day absence and a recent record showing late fading in longer trips is worth noting before trusting her to last home.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five outings, Marhaba Ghaiyyath disappointed when tried in cheekpieces at Newmarket last time out. He is effective over this distance and acts on a sound surface; an easing mark provides a small platform, though a much improved showing is needed.

runners_data.name: High Degree
runners_data.note: Haggas-trained 4yo with a smart recent second over 10f on good ground and strong prominent-style form; 17 days since last run keeps her race-fit, and this trip looks right at the upper end of her optimal range but the handicap mark of OR 92 is workable.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and dependable, High Degree performed to his level in a competitive handicap at Sandown last time, beaten two lengths off this mark. He acts on any going and handles this distance well; as our top-rated runner, he looks the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Two B Tanned
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good ground on last winning start and wears headgear (hp); Camacho's five-year-old has a big good-ground strike-rate (6W from 15 similar-going runs) and the prominent position she can naturally secure is ideal for this controlled pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Two B Tanned won here off a mark 8lb lower on her penultimate outing but has disappointed since stepping up in class, and the current mark looks stiff. First-time hood and cheekpieces add uncertainty; front-running tactics suit, but she needs to find significantly more.

runners_data.name: Pandemonium
runners_data.note: Has winning form on good ground and is a natural front-runner for Crisford — but with five prominent types contesting fewer available slots, he is likely to be shuffled wider and later than he wants, which materially undermines his winning chance here.
runners_data.comment: Pandemonium was beaten a short-head off a 2lb lower mark at this course and distance last time — a clear confidence booster. Cheekpieces may help him stay focused, though idling when asked to win is a known concern at this trip.

runners_data.name: Strength Of Spirit
runners_data.note: Burke's three-year-old has placed prominently on good ground before but sits in midfield on the map because there is simply no room for another forward-going type; his style-fit score reflects the squeeze, and he needs things to fall right from an awkward position.
runners_data.comment: Returned to form when beaten a neck off 85 last time — just 2lb below today's mark — a solid benchmark. He stays this trip, handles the going, and his trainer won this race last year; the mark is tight, but there is encouragement here.

runners_data.name: Dwindling Funds
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's five-year-old ran only 11 days ago and wears headgear (p); a genuine prominent racer who has been displaced from his favoured slot by the volume of pace horses in this field — his low OR of 76 gives a weight pull but the tactical compromise is real.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Ayr on his latest outing, Dwindling Funds at least showed a more encouraging shape and today's conditions look more suitable. He handles this trip, a top course trainer provides encouragement, and first-time cheekpieces add interest, though he faces a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Monoceros
runners_data.note: Jardine's three-year-old has winning form on good ground at 7f and shown ability to place prominently, but like the other reshuffled types is unlikely to access his natural berth here; his short trip profile over 1m1f is also a mild concern.
runners_data.comment: Held without threatening over this trip at this course last time, Monoceros has questions to answer at the distance despite pedigree suggesting he will be suited by it in time. He acts on the going and has shown ability, but this trip remains a challenge.

runners_data.name: Haayimm
runners_data.note: Bethell's lightly-raced three-year-old has only three runs but includes a win on soft and a placed effort on good ground; Tudhope in the saddle is a big plus at Musselburgh, and the horse's handy style from a small sample suggests he can slot into the key second or third spot.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a neck in a novice at Hamilton last time, Haayimm showed real tenacity and has the attitude to compete despite a demanding opening mark. He handles this distance and today's conditions; the mark is the main question, but he is unexposed and capable of more.

runners_data.name: Rochfortbridge
runners_data.note: Keatley's hold-up three-year-old has a 94-day absence and a single placed run on good ground from six starts; a true closer who needs a stronger gallop than this shape is likely to generate — ground-going stats (1/6 similar) offer little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Below par on his seasonal reappearance at Kempton, Rochfortbridge is a sturdy type with a good attitude and his trainer is in excellent form. Fast ground suits and he handles this trip; he has something to prove at three, but the stable's form counts in his favour.

runners_data.name: Thunder Wonder
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's hold-up four-year-old has a poor recent record (sim-going 11/15) and has been beaten well in similar conditions; needs a punishing pace to deliver a late run and this scenario is exactly what this race is unlikely to serve up.
runners_data.comment: Ideally suited by this trip and a sound surface, Thunder Wonder has fair ability but needs to relax far better than at Newmarket last time, when he ran well below his best. Conditions favour him and his mark has eased, but settling from the start is crucial.

races.paceDynamic: Marhaba Ghaiyyath is the one confirmed front-runner here and, crucially, is unlikely to face sustained pressure for the lead, meaning the pace will be set at a controlled, sustainable tempo over this 1m1f trip on good ground at Musselburgh. With no genuine rival ready to challenge her for the front, the fractions will be honest but not searching, creating a rail-hugging, rail-ground-saving advantage for whoever sits closest in behind. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-handy racers who can travel economically in second or third, make smooth headway turning in, and deploy a clean finishing effort — rather than deep closers who need a truly punishing gallop to peg back the leader. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position: Pandemonium, Strength Of Spirit, Monoceros, and Dwindling Funds are all genuine prominent racers who will be shuffled into a midfield that does not suit them, with High Degree, Two B Tanned, and Haayimm best placed to actually land the handy berths behind Marhaba Ghaiyyath.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Handy Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Marhaba Ghaiyyath sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the race is decided in the final two furlongs by the horses who travelled closest.
scenarios.body: If Marhaba Ghaiyyath sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the race is decided in the final two furlongs by the horses who travelled closest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Two B Tanned and High Degree both secure handy positions and the winner comes from the first four home turning in.
scenarios.body: If Two B Tanned and High Degree both secure handy positions and the winner comes from the first four home turning in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Marhaba Ghaiyyath's uncontested lead translates into a soft-pedalling gallop that no hold-up horse can bridge.
scenarios.body: If Marhaba Ghaiyyath's uncontested lead translates into a soft-pedalling gallop that no hold-up horse can bridge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Swoops Succeed
scenarios.trigger: If hidden pressure in the midfield pack causes early scrimmaging that lifts the tempo, leaving the front rank vulnerable to closers in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If hidden pressure in the midfield pack causes early scrimmaging that lifts the tempo, leaving the front rank vulnerable to closers in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Watch Haayimm's early positioning — if Daniel Tudhope slots him into second or third behind Marhaba Ghaiyyath in the first furlong, he immediately becomes the most dangerous threat in the dominant race shape.

Monitor the scrimmage for prominent spots in the opening furlong: Pandemonium, Strength Of Spirit, Monoceros, and Dwindling Funds are all likely to crowd the same ground, potentially causing interference or forcing some to check and lose position entirely.

If Marhaba Ghaiyyath shows any sign of being headed or pressured in the first half-mile, the pace dynamic shifts sharply and the probability of Scenario A collapses — track her lead margin at the 6f pole.

Two B Tanned's headgear (hood/cheekpieces) and high good-ground win rate make her one to monitor at the draw and in the preliminary canter — if she loads and jumps cleanly she is well-placed to land a prominent berth.

Rochfortbridge and Thunder Wonder are the only true hold-up horses in the field; if neither can be placed in the first five turning for home given the controlled pace, their finishing effort will be academic and can be safely discounted on running.

races.name: Max Recycle Handicap

runners_data.name: Rajstar
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse that returned a 1/6f win on Standard but has 0 wins and 0 places from 2 runs on Good; Ben Haslam yard has decent recent strike rate (2/14 in 14 days) and 12-day turnaround is sharp, but the going profile is a mild concern and 7f here tests his closing ability against minimal pace.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Ripon 12 days ago in a performance that may have served as a comeback run after a break; won at 6f to 7f and has handled fast ground, with ability still to demonstrate — the trainer's yard has been finding form hard to come by of late.

runners_data.name: Classy Clarets
runners_data.note: Carries the best recent Good-ground form in the field with 1 win and 4 places from 6 similar-going runs; racing closer to the pace than its natural position due to the overcrowded hold-up group, which is a small positive in this low-tempo shape — Jack Nicholls (5) takes 5lb off and Iain Jardine is firing at 9/34 in the last fortnight.
runners_data.comment: Set a strong front-running pace last time and nearly got away with it, fading only close home when beaten two lengths off this same mark; first-time hood could aid focus, the trainer is in good shape, and the mark is fair — a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Defence Missile
runners_data.note: Winless and low-placed across 9 outings on Good or Standard ground (0W2P from 12), and its best form has come on Soft; David Allan rides for Linda Perratt who has had a quiet 14 days (0/10), and this horse's back-of-the-pack instincts are entirely at odds with the uncontested lone-leader shape this race is producing.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Ayr 11 days ago on soft ground, a surface that does not appear to suit him, having struggled for form through much of last season; acts at 7f to 8f on good ground or an artificial surface, but plenty remains to prove.

runners_data.name: Cotai Starlight
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with only 3 runs to assess, returning after a 69-day absence which is the longest layoff in the field and a definite flag; went 5/7f Good last time and has 1 place from 3 similar-going starts — Sam James is capable but the fitness question looms large at 132lbs.
runners_data.comment: Held without threatening in a novice at Catterick 69 days ago, with little to show from her brief career so far; a wind operation is on record and faster going today should suit her action, but she remains very much one to prove herself.

runners_data.name: Willowinghurn
runners_data.note: Previously wore headgear (p) suggesting quirks, and the 15-run Good/Soft record reads 1W5P with a most recent effort of 12th over this exact trip and course combination; Daniel Tudhope is among the better jockeys here but the horse's form profile over 7f on Good is uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Beaten over eight lengths at Doncaster 16 days ago, appearing to have been ridden too prominently for her own good in that race; first-time cheekpieces and an easing mark are positives, and she has the ability to go better — returning to form is the key question.

runners_data.name: Monhammer
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran with 0 wins from 10 Good/Soft runs but 3 places; recorded a solid 2nd over 7f Good in recent history and Andrew Mullen knows this horse well — naturally races from behind which this single-pacer tempo does not ideally suit, though experience and a straightforward track could help it find its stride.
runners_data.comment: Third in a classified race at Ayr 10 days ago, going within three lengths of the winner after pulling keenly through the early stages; acts at 7f on good to soft or good to firm, but the official mark looks tight and he has yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Due Respect
runners_data.note: Listed as NON-RUNNER — no analysis applicable; was a natural hold-up horse with a poor record on Good ground (0W2P from 15) and its absence fractionally eases the redistribution pressure behind the pace.

runners_data.name: Sanditon
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard last time out and has placed once from 15 Good/Standard runs — form context shows its best efforts came on artificial surfaces, not Good turf; Rowan Scott rides for Charlie Johnston who is active at 9/76, but this horse's profile may suit a stronger pace than Ramon Di Loria is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Third at Catterick eight days ago, going within two lengths of the winner off this exact official mark at 7f, with today's ground and trip both suiting; in solid form and first-time cheekpieces could provide added edge — he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Coconut Bay
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old with 2 wins and 6 places from 15 Good/Soft runs, giving it the most experienced similar-going profile in the field; Jason Hart is a reliable northern jockey and Tristan Davidson has shown recent form (3/11 in 14 days), though the horse's natural rear-of-field instincts are being compressed forward by this race's overcrowded hold-up group.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Carlisle 22 days ago, going down by over nine lengths in a performance well short of expectations; handles 7f to 8f on a sound surface and the mark has dropped, but a much-improved effort would be needed to get involved here.

runners_data.name: Ramon Di Loria
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine front-runner and confirmed pace-setter, giving him an uncontested lead over a flat 7f Musselburgh track on Good ground; Greg Fairley partners for Ewan Whillans (1/14 last 14 days) and while the Style Fit tag reflects that a prominent role at 7f stretches his comfort zone, the absence of any rival to challenge him for the lead is a significant practical advantage.
runners_data.comment: Beaten six lengths at Carlisle 15 days ago in his second run back on turf, unable to match his better performances on an artificial surface; handles this trip on any going, prefers cut in the ground, and the mark keeps easing — but turf form this season has been disappointing.

races.paceDynamic: Ramon Di Loria is the sole confirmed front-runner in this ten-runner 7f handicap at Musselburgh, and with no genuine rival to push him for the lead, he is set to bowl along at a controlled, self-selected tempo on Good ground. That uncontested lead over a flat, fair track creates a straightforward rail-hugging gallop rather than a true test of stamina, meaning the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to soften up the closers significantly. The field behind him is saturated with hold-up horses — Sanditon, Defence Missile, Classy Clarets, Monhammer, Due Respect and Coconut Bay are all natural wait-and-pounce types who cannot all find their preferred position, so several will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would like, masking their true profile. This race shape — a lone, unchallenged leader setting a modest gallop — materially favours prominent and close-tracking types who can sit just off Ramon Di Loria and strike at the two-furlong pole, rather than genuine hold-up horses asked to produce a closing burst from deep against minimal pace injection.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria dictates unchallenged and sets a comfortable, honest tempo that rewards track-position.
scenarios.body: If Ramon Di Loria dictates unchallenged and sets a comfortable, honest tempo that rewards track-position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close-Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If a handful of hold-up horses redistribute forward and push the early pace, elevating the gallop enough to bring one late charger into play.
scenarios.body: If a handful of hold-up horses redistribute forward and push the early pace, elevating the gallop enough to bring one late charger into play.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria sets a falsely slow early gallop that gives him so much in hand that he simply outstays all rivals.
scenarios.body: If Ramon Di Loria sets a falsely slow early gallop that gives him so much in hand that he simply outstays all rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Trouble
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded hold-up section causes traffic issues and interference in the straight, opening the door for an unexpected beneficiary.
scenarios.body: If the overcrowded hold-up section causes traffic issues and interference in the straight, opening the door for an unexpected beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Ramon Di Loria sets the entire pace dynamic — if he is slow away or is challenged unexpectedly in the first furlong, the shape collapses entirely and hold-up horses redistribute further forward than anticipated.

Classy Clarets, Defence Missile, Monhammer, Sanditon and Coconut Bay are all natural closers compressing into a limited midfield space; watch for scrimmaging and bumping as the field settles behind the leader, particularly in the first two furlongs.
Cotai Starlight returns after 69 days off and is the most unknown fitness quantity in the race — if it dwells or tires rapidly from the rear it becomes an obstacle in a congested field.

Due Respect is listed as a non-runner — connections of other runners should confirm the final field size before assessing position in the draw and stall allocation, as its withdrawal slightly reduces the hold-up horse congestion.

Good ground is confirmed throughout the card at Musselburgh and is consistent across all seven races — no hidden surface variation to factor in, but the forecast should be monitored for any late-afternoon change ahead of this 3:30 slot.

races.name: Racing TV Profits Returned To Racing Handicap

runners_data.name: Son
runners_data.note: A consistent hold-up performer in 7f Good-ground handicaps with three places from five similar-going runs; David Allan rides for the in-form Tim Easterby yard and this trip and surface are spot-on, though he needs at least a fair pace to reel rivals in.
runners_data.comment: Third at York 17 days ago in a performance that matched his best level, beaten just over two lengths off this official mark on a sound surface at his ideal 7f trip; yet to win in recent starts but rates well clear of the field and is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Abduction
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who won over 7f Good for Jim Goldie recently, giving him strong claims on course form; Jake Dickson's 7lb claim is a meaningful weight reducer, though his closing style means he is reliant on enough tempo being set ahead of him.
runners_data.comment: Won here in April by a head off this exact official mark, and came within two lengths of the winner in his most recent start; effective at 7f to 8f on any going, with a workable mark and the trainer in good form at this course — the main concern is consistency.

runners_data.name: Ameilya
runners_data.note: 399-day absence is a significant flag for a horse who has been running at middle-distances on softer ground — the step back to 7f Good on a tight track is a big ask on return, and while Stuart Coltherd sends runners fit enough, her tendency to race from off the pace will be harder to execute than the map position suggests.
runners_data.comment: Off the track for nearly 400 days and last seen below her best in a claimer in Ireland, performing poorly on both the Flat and over obstacles through the past year; showed ability at this trip on good ground earlier in her career, but there is a great deal to prove here.

runners_data.name: Gressington
runners_data.note: Blinkered for the first time today which could sharpen her early response, but her six recent runs show zero wins or places on Good ground; Jason Hart's typically enterprising style may help her position better than her figures suggest, though the form line reads poorly.
runners_data.comment: A laboured effort at Thirsk 14 days ago, beaten six lengths, and form throughout recent starts has been difficult; handles 6f to 8f on a sound surface and first-time blinkers are worth noting, though a significant step forward is still needed here.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: In-form mare who has won twice and placed three times from her last five starts at six furlongs, but today's step up to seven furlongs on a track that suits resolute galloping types may stretch her; her natural rear-of-field tendency will be squeezed by field size, though Rowan Scott rides her in good form.
runners_data.comment: Won at Hamilton five days ago, taking a handicap by over two lengths off a 5lb lower mark, having built on each run in recent starts; acts on any going, handles the trip, and first-time blinkers add an interesting element — the form is going the right way.

runners_data.name: Diamont Katie
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: K R Burke's four-year-old has placed four times and won once from nine similar-going runs and has shown consistent front-running ability over the trip; Clifford Lee will attempt to dictate from the front and, uncontested, she could prove difficult to peg back.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at her last start, beaten four lengths off this same official mark despite being supported in the market, which was slightly below expectations; has been in improved form since a wind operation, and a return to her better level here cannot be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Native Instinct
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride for Edward Bethell after a 43-day break, and the horse has placed three times from seven similar-going runs over this trip; a prominent racer who naturally sits just off the pace, he will want to avoid being trapped wide in a race with several horses seeking the same position.
runners_data.comment: Beaten seven lengths at Carlisle 43 days ago when soft ground appeared beyond him; quicker conditions today look a genuine plus, and the mark is now more manageable, though the trainer's yard has struggled for results recently and a return to form is needed.

runners_data.name: The Gay Blade
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's seven-year-old has won four of his last six starts including two successive 7f Good victories and carries obvious claims on recent form; Andrew Mullen knows the horse well and his ability to race prominently and finish with authority makes him the most complete profile in the race for this shape.
runners_data.comment: Three wins on the bounce and landed a handicap at Ayr last time by two lengths off a 6lb lower mark on soft, despite idling close home; acts on any going at 6f to 7f and is clearly thriving, though the mark has climbed sharply.

races.paceDynamic: Diamont Katie is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Native Instinct and The Gay Blade as genuine prominent types, there is enough pace to establish a clear leader without it becoming a true burn-up — Diamont Katie can roll along at a fair but sustainable clip on good ground over seven furlongs at Musselburgh. The prominent runners will press for their positions early but none is likely to strike an extreme tempo, meaning the race is set up for those able to travel close to the pace and quicken from there rather than those needing a strong gallop to close into. This field holds more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Ameilya, Gressington, and Iris Dancer are genuine closers but will find themselves squeezed into midfield against their natural grain, diluting their effectiveness. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers and well-positioned hold-up horses who can secure a ground-saving pitch, as the anticipated honest-but-not-extreme pace rewards those travelling in the first four rather than those forced to make up ground from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Control
scenarios.trigger: If Diamont Katie leads at a fair pace and the prominent trio dictate terms throughout the seven furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Diamont Katie leads at a fair pace and the prominent trio dictate terms throughout the seven furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace lifts sufficiently in the middle stages to string the field out and create a genuine closing opportunity.
scenarios.body: If the pace lifts sufficiently in the middle stages to string the field out and create a genuine closing opportunity.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front runners do not truly commit to the pace and the race develops into a slow-run tactical affair with a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: If the front runners do not truly commit to the pace and the race develops into a slow-run tactical affair with a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If early position battles cause interference or crowding, unsettling the prominent movers and gifting a clean run to an overlooked runner.
scenarios.body: If early position battles cause interference or crowding, unsettling the prominent movers and gifting a clean run to an overlooked runner.

watchPoints.text: The Gay Blade has won four of his last six races with two consecutive 7f Good wins — his prominent style perfectly suits this shape and he arrives with the strongest recent winning form in the field.

Diamont Katie's willingness to bowl along in front unchallenged is the key pace variable — if she is allowed to establish a comfortable rhythm without pressure, those trailing her face a very stiff task to close.

Ameilya's 399-day absence combined with a drop back from middle distances to 7f on a track she has not run at recently makes her a significant risk to any scenario that depends on her running to form.

Native Instinct's 43-day break and Daniel Tudhope's booking is worth monitoring in the market — Tudhope rarely takes rides without cause and the horse has placed three times on similar ground at this trip.

Gressington runs in blinkers for the first time today — first-time headgear can sharpen early pace and may cause her to break quicker than expected, potentially disrupting the front-running shape if she takes a keener early position than anticipated.

races.name: Catherine & Charlotte Roche Handicap

runners_data.name: Gemini Man
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has won his last two and landed a 12f good-ground contest recently; Iain Jardine sends him back after just 8 days, signalling confidence, and his front-running profile is uniquely suited to this shape — lone leader on flat good ground over a staying trip is his optimal scenario, though the step to 1m4½f is worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Three wins from his last five starts, most recently landing a handicap here by a neck off a 4lb lower mark, outstaying the field; consistent over 10-12f on this ground and the trainer is in form — the mark has tightened but he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Sophiesticate
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type partnered by claimer Kyle McHugh (7lb), and her recent form of 77-763 over 12f on good ground offers little encouragement; trainer R Mike Smith is without a winner from 14 runners in the past fortnight, and Sophiesticate's tendency to fill the minor placings without threatening is a pattern here.
runners_data.comment: Showed an improved effort over course and distance last time, going down by just half a length off this same official mark at extended 12f; this trip clearly agrees with her and conditions suit, though she is yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Is She Now
runners_data.note: Bounced back to winning form over 13f on soft 11 days ago under David Nolan, and the step up to 1m4½f looks tailor-made for a genuine stayer; her going record on good (18th of 18 on one occasion) is a concern, though that outlier aside she has placed on similar ground and Daragh Bourke's yard is active and in form.
runners_data.comment: Returned to winning form at Ayr 11 days ago, landing a classified race on the Flat by four lengths, which shows she is back in good order; effective at this trip and handles the going, though handicap company is a tougher ask — the mark looks fair.

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura
runners_data.note: Four-year-old whose form string is littered with mid-pack finishes and a noted tendency to fade; though shown in midfield here, Storm On Jura's instinct is to sit well off the pace, and the redistribution reflects a saturated hold-up group rather than any natural stalking ability — poor recent form (6th, 9th, 11th) on good ground compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: A disappointing display at Hamilton 13 days ago, beaten 10 lengths, adding to a run of below-par efforts; her trainer does have a strong record at this track, but she has yet to produce any consistent showings and remains hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's four-year-old wears a visor and has placed twice over 12-13f on good ground, including a runner-up at this distance on good going recently — the form figures 068242 show genuine consistency without a win; Jason Hart takes the ride, and while Falaise Blanc's true instinct is to come from behind, the placed form at this trip and in this going gives it more substance than its stablemates in the hold-up group.
runners_data.comment: Placed second at Hamilton just five days ago, going within seven lengths of the winner at this trip and running to his current level; first-time visor adds interest and the mark looks fair, though he is yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: On The Bubble
runners_data.note: Greg Fairley partners this five-year-old whose entire recent form has been over 8-9f — the step to 1m4½f is a significant and untested jump in trip; a natural closer by style, On The Bubble has place form on good ground but Gary Rutherford's yard has drawn a blank from three runners in the past fortnight, and the distance query is the dominant concern here.
runners_data.comment: A lacklustre showing here last time, going down by five and a quarter lengths, with form having been patchy throughout recent starts; handles cut in the ground but may not appreciate the faster conditions today, and much improvement is needed.

races.paceDynamic: Gemini Man is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 1m4½f handicap at Musselburgh and, with no rival willing or able to press him, he will stride into a clear lead from the outset and control every fraction on good ground. The remainder of the field — Sophiesticate, Is She Now, Storm On Jura, Falaise Blanc, and On The Bubble — are all natural hold-up types, meaning the pace behind Gemini Man will be orderly and unhurried, creating a single-file procession rather than a contested gallop. This race shape strongly favours front-running and prominent profiles: a lone leader dictating a fair but unforced tempo on flat, good ground over a staying trip is the classic setup for a wire-to-wire performance. This field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Storm On Jura, Falaise Blanc, and On The Bubble are all true closers redistributed to midfield, but none are natural stalkers who will sit on Gemini Man's girth and apply pressure; that is precisely what makes his position so valuable today.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gemini Man Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Gemini Man sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop and the hold-up brigade fail to mount a coordinated challenge.
scenarios.body: If Gemini Man sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop and the hold-up brigade fail to mount a coordinated challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stayer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Gemini Man's solo lead sets a true enough gallop that a genuine stayer picks him off inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Gemini Man's solo lead sets a true enough gallop that a genuine stayer picks him off inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Ambushes
scenarios.trigger: If a midfield-mapped horse manoeuvres into second or third early and launches a challenge entering the straight.
scenarios.body: If a midfield-mapped horse manoeuvres into second or third early and launches a challenge entering the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Finish, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses early or traffic issues scramble the midfield order in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses early or traffic issues scramble the midfield order in the straight.

watchPoints.text: Watch Gemini Man's early stride rate — if Andrew Mullen sends him clear immediately and no rival responds, the race could be over as a contest by the home turn, with the only question being whether the 1m4½f trip stretches him.

Monitor Is She Now in the straight — David Nolan will be angling for a late run, and if Gemini Man's lead compresses inside the final two furlongs, her proven stamina over 13f makes her the most credible threat.

Falaise Blanc is the hold-up runner with the best positional form at this distance on good going; if Jason Hart manages to avoid traffic in the midfield bunch, a sustained challenge from two furlongs out is possible rather than a one-paced late rattle.

Storm On Jura's noted tendency to fade in finishes is a significant red flag in a race where the closers must travel further than usual before striking — watch for the classic pattern of a prominent enough early position that still evaporates in the straight.

The claimer allowance (Kyle McHugh 7lb on Sophiesticate) is only meaningful if Sophiesticate can get into a challenging position; given her hold-up style in a race already packed with rear-runners, watch whether she simply never gets into a competitive berth.

races.name: Watch On Racing TV Handicap

runners_data.name: Invincible Crown
runners_data.note: True hold-up sprinter for Ruth Carr; six runs in similar Good ground at 5f this season suggest solid course/distance fit but a best-of-placing of second tells you she wins rarely — only lands this from a chaotic scenario.
runners_data.comment: Finished second at Nottingham five days ago, going down by three-quarters of a length off this official mark on a sound surface, and handles 5f well; yet to win in recent starts, and the trainer's yard is going through a lean run.

runners_data.name: Auntie Jo
runners_data.note: Won on Standard at Carlisle last time and placed on Good, so the going is fine; natural hold-up runner who will struggle to get her desired position at the rear in this traffic-heavy field, diminishing the potency of her late effort.
runners_data.comment: Won at this trip and goes well on the going, making her competitive at this mark; wore blinkers at her last start but pulled across track in the closing stages, finishing fifth beaten four lengths off this same mark — temperament is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Race-defining runner — confirmed front-runner for Jim Goldie whose recent 5f Good-ground form includes two wins and a consistent placed record; the amateur rider Amie Waugh (3) will need to judge the pace correctly, but with no other confirmed front-runner she has a golden opportunity to control this race from flag to finish.
runners_data.comment: Narrow runner-up here just eight days ago, going down by a neck off this same official mark on a sound surface, and the trip clearly suits; in solid form coming into this, wears a first-time hood, and lines up from draw 8.

runners_data.name: Data Fata Secutus
runners_data.note: Tudhope takes the mount for Rebecca Menzies on this 3yo who ran second over this C&D trip on Good last time; form-line is noisy but that C&D second is the key line and positioning just off Wee Mary's heels would suit.
runners_data.comment: Beaten seven lengths at Redcar last time over 6f, a trip that appeared beyond her, and the drop to 5f here looks a genuine improvement for her chances; first-time cheekpieces add interest, though she is yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo for Gemma Tutty who has placed on Good ground at 5f but is working off a limited evidence base; 19 days fresh, and her best effort (third of four runners) came on Good, so conditions are not a concern — still unexposed.
runners_data.comment: Fourth on her handicap debut at Catterick, beaten nine lengths on easy ground, and there is plenty still to prove at this level; handles 5f and should appreciate a firmer surface today, but she remains without a win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Sands Of Seve
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and is a true hold-up horse mapped into midfield; 57 days since last run is a flag, and his best form has come on Standard surfaces — zero wins or places on Good ground in the historical record is a meaningful concern.
runners_data.comment: Well below his best at Bath most recently, finishing down the field 57 days ago, and a significant step up in form is needed; tends to travel prominently and acts on artificial surfaces, with first-time visor fitted and lines up from draw 9.

runners_data.name: What A Tahoo
runners_data.note: Won over 5f Good last time out and has three additional top-three finishes in recent starts — the most in-form horse by raw results; natural hold-up runner who the map has pushed forward, so the real question is whether Cam Hardie can find the right position to deploy that finishing kick from further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Won at Ripon 13 days ago, getting the better of the field by a length off a lower official mark in a smooth display at 5f; the trip and ground both suit her, and she is clearly in form — the one to beat from draw 10.

runners_data.name: Bonito Cavalo
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Jim Goldie tagged as fading in finish, which is damning in a sprint; 78 days off the track, best form came on Standard surfaces, and the redistribution into midfield only worsens his chance — hard to make a case.
runners_data.comment: Beaten seven lengths at Newcastle 78 days ago, with form having deteriorated across recent starts; acts at this trip and handles different surfaces, though he clearly thrives more on artificial tracks, making today a harder ask and hard to recommend at this level.

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Veteran 8yo for Linda Perratt with genuine Good-ground experience (10 runs, one win, six places on similar going), so conditions suit better than most here; a natural hold-up horse forced into midfield, meaning his usual closing position is taken away, but his course familiarity is real.
runners_data.comment: Performed to his current level here just eight days ago, finishing third and going within two lengths of the leader off this exact official mark, with 5f as his best trip; first-time cheekpieces add an interesting angle, though a small further step is still needed.

runners_data.name: Hard Nut
runners_data.note: Oldest horse in the field at nine for Linda Perratt, with an apprentice aboard; best recent Going form was on Soft rather than Good, and the field is stacked enough that this redistribution into midfield from a true hold-up style leaves him with too much to do.
runners_data.comment: A below-par showing here last time, beaten seven lengths, with form having gone backwards over recent starts; he acts over 5f and handles a sound surface, but a significant improvement on recent efforts would be needed to get involved.

races.paceDynamic: Wee Mary is the confirmed pace-setter here, likely to stride into a clear lead from the gates on a flat, uncontested Musselburgh 5f, setting a sustainable rather than suicidal tempo given she is racing alone at the front. With no other genuine front-runner to challenge her, she will control the fractions throughout, meaning the race is unlikely to be truly honest from end to end and the advantage flows towards those racing just off the pace rather than those coming from far back. The field contains a significant excess of hold-up types — Auntie Jo, Sands Of Seve, What A Tahoo, Bonito Cavalo, Sixcor and Hard Nut are all true hold-up horses pushed into the midfield/prominent positions on the map because the rear of the field is overcrowded, meaning their natural closing kick will be compromised. This shape — one controlled front-runner, a bunch of reluctant hold-up types unable to get to the back — clearly favours horses who can genuinely sit second or third and pounce, or Wee Mary herself if she is allowed to dictate unopposed at a manageable gallop.

scenarios.title: Wee Mary Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Wee Mary bowls along comfortably in front and the hold-up brigade fail to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: If Wee Mary bowls along comfortably in front and the hold-up brigade fail to close the gap in time.

scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting second or third tracks Wee Mary and produces a decisive move inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If a horse sitting second or third tracks Wee Mary and produces a decisive move inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Gets Lucky Late
scenarios.trigger: If Wee Mary goes too fast early or falters, opening a lane for a strong finisher to rattle through.
scenarios.body: If Wee Mary goes too fast early or falters, opening a lane for a strong finisher to rattle through.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Pace Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded midfield causes interference early and multiple hold-up types lose position through crowding.
scenarios.body: If the overcrowded midfield causes interference early and multiple hold-up types lose position through crowding.

watchPoints.text: Wee Mary's early gallop sets the tempo for the entire race — if Amie Waugh (3) misjudges and goes too fast, the hold-up horses scrambling from midfield could get closer than expected and undermine Scenario A entirely.

Six genuine hold-up types (Auntie Jo, Sands Of Seve, What A Tahoo, Bonito Cavalo, Sixcor, Hard Nut) will be jostling for the same midfield slots in the early strides — watch for crowding, bumping and any horse being badly shuffled back.

What A Tahoo is the most in-form horse in the race on raw results but is a natural hold-up runner; if Cam Hardie can manufacture a prominent position rather than accepting midfield, it transforms his chance significantly.

Sands Of Seve's 57-day absence is the longest in the field and his visor headgear suggests a horse that needs a gear-change in focus — monitor in the paddock and first furlong for any signs of ring-rustiness.

Data Fata Secutus is the only runner with a confirmed C&D placed run on Good ground this season — Daniel Tudhope's ability to slot into second behind Wee Mary early could prove decisive if Scenario B unfolds.
